newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-BOSMAN FINED 10,000 RAND FOR WEIR KICK.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-BOSMAN FINED 10,000 RAND FOR WEIR KICK.

text.p: Mpumalanga lock forward Marius Bosman was fined 10,000 rand ($2,230) by a provincial disciplinary committee on Monday for aiming the kick which ended Doddie Weir's British Lions tour of South Africa.

Fellow Mpumalanga player Elandre van den Bergh, who raked Scottish loose forward Rob Wainwright in broken play in the same match, was fined 5,000 rand by the committee - although 3,000 rand of his fine was suspended until the end of the year.
"These are the severest punishments ever handed out to a player by our union," said Mpumalanga Rugby Union chief executive Willem Strauss.
"Our disciplinary committee found that the two players had brought both our union and the game into disrepute," Strauss added in a statement after a one-hour meeting.

Both Bosman and van den Bergh were found guilty of dangerous play during last Wednesday's match between the British Lions and the Mpumalanga Pumas. Both incidents resulted in penalties for the Lions on the field of play.
Scotland lock Weir was ruled out of the remainder of the tour after being kicked on the knee by Bosman during a maul and tearing ligaments. He was replaced by England's Nigel Redman.
